title: iTransformer: Variate-token attention scales sub-quadratically in the number of features on Electricity, Traffic, Weather
abstract: We study long-horizon multivariate forecasting using iTransformer, a inverted transformer treating variates as tokens. On Electricity, Traffic, Weather, at horizon 336, Variate-token attention scales sub-quadratically in the number of features on Electricity, Traffic, Weather. iTransformer attention cost grows with the number of variates rather than the input length, saving 15% memory at length 1024. We discuss two limitations: Evaluation is restricted to public benchmarks and may not reflect production settings. Reported gains use a single held-out split; results across seeds vary by more than the headline MSE difference. Future work should address extending the evaluation to include dlinear and nlinear as baselines. and reporting per-seed variance and confidence intervals for the headline metric.
